name: Separation

related.relation: Both split the swarm into classes; in separation the classes are fixed by hidden colours, in $k$-grouping and partitioning they are chosen by the robots.

summary: Robots of different (hidden) colours must separate so that each colour class occupies its own region.
statement: Each robot has a fixed colour that the others can see but it cannot (an *unconscious* robot). The robots must arrange themselves so that the colour classes are separated (into points, lines or circles, depending on the variant).

primer.intro: Imagine a party where each guest wears a coloured hat they cannot see, but they can see everybody else's hat, and nobody may speak. The guests must sort themselves so that all red hats stand on one line, all blue hats on another, and so on. In the separation problem $n$ point robots in the plane each have a fixed colour that the others see but they cannot (an *unconscious* robot). In the basic version robots are oblivious (they forget everything after each move), see everybody, agree on the direction of one axis, and are activated by an asynchronous (ASYNC) adversary: a robot may look while others are still moving. They must end up separated into parallel lines, one colour class per line.

ideas.title: Others tell you where to go
ideas.idea:
The key difficulty is that a robot does not know its own colour, but every other robot does. One way out, used with opaque robots (robots that block the view of robots behind them) under SSYNC:
1. Bring all robots to the lower half of a circle, where everybody can see everybody.
2. Divide this semicircle into sectors, one per colour.
3. A few chosen robots act as signallers: by moving to a carefully chosen point they encode "the robot of colour $c$ at this position should go to sector $j$".
4. The robot addressed reads the signal and moves to its sector, without ever learning its colour directly.
5. Finally each sector is moved onto its own semicircle, so colour classes lie on concentric semicircles.
ideas.analysis: Positions are the only way robots can pass information, so the algorithm turns positions into messages. [Pyati2026Separation] reach concentric semicircles in $O(n)$ epochs (an epoch is a stretch of time in which every robot completes at least one cycle) without collisions and without knowing $n$. We read only a summary of this paper's arXiv version, so the steps above give the idea, not its details. The algorithms for the standard ASYNC variant are different and are not described here.
ideas.why_it_matters: Using movement as a message channel is how silent robots share information they cannot sense themselves, the same idea behind signalling with lights.

ideas.title: A colour with only one robot
ideas.idea: Asynchronous separation into parallel lines is solvable when robots share one axis, provided no colour class has a single robot. If some robot is the only one of its colour, [Flocchini2025Separation] show that no algorithm works. The proof is a symmetry argument in the paper and is not reproduced here.
ideas.analysis: The catalogue records the condition but not its proof, and we have not read the full text. A student should take away the shape of the result: solvability depends on how many robots share each colour, because a robot can learn about its own colour only from what the other robots do.
ideas.why_it_matters: It marks the exact boundary between possible and impossible for the asynchronous algorithm of [Flocchini2025Separation].

history: Separation of unconscious coloured robots asked whether robots that **cannot see their own colour** can still sort themselves by colour, first synchronously [Seike2023Separation], then asynchronously [Flocchini2025Separation] and with opaque robots [Pyati2026Separation].

measures.name: Time
measures.description: rounds (FSYNC, SSYNC) or epochs (ASYNC) until the task is done; "finite" when only solvability is known

measures.name: Colours
measures.description: colours of the light per robot (0 for oblivious robots)

variants.title: ASYNC, one common axis
variants.summary: Robots that carry a colour visible to others but not to themselves separate by colour into parallel lines, under ASYNC, if they share one axis.

preconditions: if some robot is uniquely coloured

colours.note: The colours are given, not chosen.

variants.title: Opaque robots, SSYNC
variants.summary: Opaque unconscious robots separate into concentric semicircles in $O(n)$ epochs.

figure.caption: Separation: each robot carries a fixed colour that the others see but it cannot; the robots must arrange themselves so that the colour classes are separated, into parallel lines in the standard ASYNC setting [Seike2023Separation]. The animation sketches the SSYNC algorithm for opaque robots [Pyati2026Separation] (read in summary only): the robots move to a semicircle, one sector per colour; a signaller points at a misplaced robot, which then moves to its sector; finally each colour class moves onto its own concentric semicircle.
